title: Standardize open-model intake flow, version pinning, and compatibility notes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify and lock the acceptance criteria, metadata requirements, and UI/API behavior for onboarding new open-source model variants into the Model Catalog. The goal is to remove ambiguity for engineering and community contributors about what metadata and compatibility guarantees are required; define how version pinning and fallback to compatible variants will be surfaced to customers; and create a minimal validation checklist that centralizes security, perf and contract checks used by the onboarding pipeline.
background: We have several bespoke intake practices for community models (example: ad-hoc notes in PRs, inconsistent version pinning guidance, and varying 'compatible_with' metadata). This leads to customer confusion when models unexpectedly change behavior after a registry update and creates operational risk for Redwood when we autoswitch or fall back models. PMs, runtime, and catalog engineers need a clear spec so onboarding is predictable and automated validation can be added to the onboarding pipeline.
scope_in: Authoritative metadata schema for open models (fields and allowed values)
Version pinning UX/API semantics (pin, soft-pin, unpinned) and fallback behavior rules
Compatibility notes format and enforcement level (informational vs. blocking)
A minimal automated validation checklist (basic security scan, license check, basic perf signal) to gate merge into catalog staging
Acceptance criteria for catalog UI and public API to display pin/status/compatibility
scope_out: Automated performance benchmarking harness (this will be a follow-up ticket)
Full KMS/HSM onboarding flow for private deployments
Migration of legacy internal-only model entries (handled separately)
acceptance_criteria: A single JSON schema (and markdown doc) exists that lists required metadata keys for open models and allowed value types; schema is stored in repo: /catalog/schemas/open_model_v1.json
API behavior: POST /catalog/models with metadata including 'pin_mode' accepts values ['pin','soft-pin','unpin'] and returns a deterministic response describing fallback policy
UI: Model details page shows pin status, last pinned version, and explicit compatibility notes section; mock approved by Design

Onboarding validation: PRs that register open models must pass the minimal checks (license present and recognized, metadata schema validation, basic token-size perf smoke < 2x baseline) to be merged into staging branch

Compatibility guidance: when 'compatible_with' is provided it must reference a specific model-family identifier; if absent, onboarding prompts the owner to provide rationale and adds 'compatibility=unknown' flag

Behavioral guarantee: If a pinned model version is available, hosted inference routes to the pinned version; for 'soft-pin' runtime may route to newer compatible builds only if they pass runtime compatibility checks; all fallbacks are logged and surface in console rollouts dashboard
test_plan: QA will validate schema enforcement by submitting example model registry entries for: 1) pinned OSS model, 2) soft-pinned model with compatible flag, 3) unpinned model with unknown compatibility. Verify API responses, assert UI displays and console logs for fallback events, and simulate runtime fallback by staging a pinned model missing artifact to confirm route logs and canary fallback.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge schema and API change behind 'catalog-intake-v2' feature flag. 2) Run 2-week staged onboarding for community contributors (invite 3 partners). 3) Flip flag for internal onboarding and monitor catalog errors and fallback metrics for 48h. 4) Full public rollout with updated docs and migration guidance.

2026-02-03 - Maya Chen: Proposed schema in github PR with required fields: id, name, license, artifacts, model_family, version, pin_mode, compatible_with, perf_baseline.
2026-02-18 - Ravi Chandra: Runtime team proposes 'soft-pin' semantic and fallback logging events shape; flagged need for runtime compatibility handshake API (ENG-2540 dependency).

2026-02-28 - Diego Alvarez: Design reviewed and provided two wireframe variants for how pin status and compatibility notes appear on the model detail page; prefers compact badge plus expandable notes.

2026-03-05 - Priya Rao (Security): Reviewed license and artifact checks; added mandatory check that artifacts originate from recognized registries or have signed provenance; flagged additional manual review for models with commercial licenses.

2026-03-10 - Luca Marin: Updated acceptance criteria to require explicit 'compatibility=unknown' marker when compatibility missing; requested sign-off from Catalog Eng and Runtime Eng to move to In Review.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter gating reduces catalog churn and runtime incidents but increases friction for community contributors; we will mitigate by publishing a clear onboarding checklist and example repo templates. If runtime compatibility handshake adds >3 weeks, we will provision a 'soft-compatibility' interim where maintainers manually certify compatibility in the onboarding PR.
qa_checklist: Schema validation passes for sample payloads
API returns explicit fallback policy in model resource
UI shows pin state and compatible_with link
Onboarding PRs are blocked on missing license field
Fallback log entries contain model_id, requested_version, routed_version, and reason
